<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->
Implement IIndicatorWarmUpPeriodProvider for PythonIndicator (#5988)
#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
- Implement IIndicatorWarmUpPeriodProvider in PythonIndicator.cs
- Add unit test in `PythonIndicatorTests.cs` to check Python indicators warms up properly 
- Add regression test to check the new feature keeps backwards compatibility with Python indicators that do not set explicitly `WarmUpPeriod` parameter
#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #5988 
#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
With this change the user will be able to warm up a custom Python Indicator
#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->
This change do not require changes or updates to the documentation
#### How Has This Been Tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
- In order to test custom Python indicators were warming up properly, it was created a custom Python Indicator setting the WarmUpPeriod paramater as the period value. Then it was created an instance of a Python indicator using the custom one and after get the WarmUpPeriod parameter it was warmed up manually, asserting the indicator was ready only when the amount of data points were bigger than the `WarmUpPeriod`.
- In order to check that the new feature kept backwards compatibility with Python indicators that do not set `WarmUpPeriod` it was made a regression test in which it was compared the values of two SMA (Simple Moving Average) custom Python indicators, where one of them set the `WarmUpPeriod` parameter, checking the values were the same for both

From #5943 

> It looks like the update to PythonNet 2.0.8 has fixed the type error, but instead we now get a different error message: 
> 
> ```
> During the algorithm initialization, the following exception has occurred: NotImplementedException : Indicator.Value must be implemented. Please implement this missing method in AverageTrueRange
>    at QuantConnect.Indicators.PythonIndicator.SetIndicator(PyObject indicator) in /LeanCloud/CI.Builder/bin/Debug/src/QuantConnect/Lean/Indicators/PythonIndicator.cs:line 114
> 
>    at QuantConnect.Indicators.PythonIndicator..ctor(PyObject indicator) in /LeanCloud/CI.Builder/bin/Debug/src/QuantConnect/Lean/Indicators/PythonIndicator.cs:line 89
> 
>    at QuantConnect.Algorithm.QCAlgorithm.WrapPythonIndicator(PyObject pyObject) in /LeanCloud/CI.Builder/bin/Debug/src/QuantConnect/Lean/Algorithm/QCAlgorithm.Python.cs:line 1266
> 
>    at QuantConnect.Algorithm.QCAlgorithm.WarmUpIndicator(Symbol symbol, PyObject indicator, Nullable`1 resolution) in /LeanCloud/CI.Builder/bin/Debug/src/QuantConnect/Lean/Algorithm/QCAlgorithm.Python.cs:line 629
> ```
> 
> The algorithm used is the same as above in the initial post. 
> I think this error is caused by #5992. For some reason the AverageTrueRange indicator is now taken to be a PythonIndicator. 
>
